chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
regarding one in Ihram who killed an ostrich. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a Badaanah (a camel or cow). So if he cannot find it, then feeding sixty poor people.'

And he said: 'If the value of the Badaanah is more than the feeding of sixty poor people, he does not exceed feeding sixty poor people; and if the value of the Badaanah is less than the feeding of sixty poor people, there is not upon him except the value of the Badaanah.'

key_terms.بَدَنَة: A mature camel or cow used as sacrificial expiation
key_terms.مُحْرِم: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for killing an ostrich while in Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details the kaffarah for killing a wild ostrich while in Ihram, establishing a flexible penalty system where the expiation is either a Badaanah (camel/cow) or feeding sixty poor people. The ruling introduces a comparative valuation principle: if the animal's market value is lower than the cost of feeding sixty poor, the owner pays the animal's value; otherwise, the penalty is capped at feeding the poor. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on fairness and economic practicality in ritual expiations, ensuring the penalty is neither excessively burdensome nor unduly lenient.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from one of our companions,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding one in Ihraam killing an ostrich. Heasws said: ‘Upon him is a sacrificial animal. So if he cannot find, the he feeds sixty poor ones’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the value of the animal was more than the feeding of sixty poor ones, it (the penalty) would not exceed feeding of sixty poor ones; and if the value of the animal was less than the feeding of sixty poor ones, it (penalty) would not be upon him except for the value of the animal’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from certain persons of our people who has said the following:
“About a man who in the state of Ihram kills an ostrich, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘He must pay one badanah; if he cannot afford then he must feed sixty destitute people.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘If the value of badanah is more than feeding sixty destitute people, it is not obligatory to feed more than sixty; if its value is less than the cost of feeding sixty destitute, he only owes the value of badanah.’”
